newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia should aim for 5 pct growth-WMC chairman.
newsitem.headline: Australia should aim for 5 pct growth-WMC chairman.

text.p: Australia should be aiming for an annual growth rate of five percent and an unemployment rate of between four and five percent, WMC Ltd chairman Sir Arvi Parbo said on Wednesday.

There was no reason why Australia should not aim at a growth rate "of say, five percent per annum and full employment for an increasing population which is essential to secure our future," Parbo told a luncheon meeting on Wednesday.
Full employment in Australia was likely to be reached at four or five percent of unemployment, he said.
Any country that could not provide meaningful employment for young people was facing a very serious problem, Parbo said.
"We are creating a large disillusioned and negatively-minded group of people amongst those on whom our very future dpends," he said.
Parbo said Australia's growth rate of about 3.5 percent was only modest and typical of an economy which was reaching maturity.
"Unless we can continue to attract younger people as immigrants, we will run into the danger of a low-growth and contracting economy," he said.
Figures released earlier on Wednesday showed average gross domestic product rose 0.9 percent in the March quarter for annual growth of 2.4 percent.
Unemployment was 8.7 percent in April and has been stuck at or above 8.5 percent for about the past year.
